newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP DIVES TWO PCT AFTER O'CONNOR RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: BHP DIVES TWO PCT AFTER O'CONNOR RESIGNS.

text.p: Shares in Australia's largest listed company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, slumped 34 cents or two percent to A$17.10 immediately after it said BHP Petroleum division chief John O'Connor had resigned because of irreconcilable differences with the board.
Analysts said O'Connor's discussion with analysts about a possible float of BHP Petroleum appeared to have brought him undone.
"In a company like BHP, anyone going outside the company framework talking about what he wanted to do and discussing that outside is pushing their luck," said one senior BHP analyst.
"From a company discipline view, it was inevitable it was going to happen," he said.
Analysts said the appearance of board and management turmoil in the wake of O'Connor's resignation and other executive resignations this week will be negative for BHP's shares in the short term.
"I'm sure it it will take a hit here and overseas tonight, but the underlying assets are good and some people will see it providing ample opportunity to buy," said one BHP analyst.
BHP's decision would add to international perceptions that much of the Australian resources sector is poorly managed, the head of an institutional dealing desk told Reuters.
"They have got rid of the one guy (O'Connor) who appeared to be the leading light there, the one businessman who appeared to be running his business in a very clean, efficient fashion," he said.
"You'd think that the international perception would be that the company is in a state of shambles."
He said the move followed Newcrest Ltd's foray into Normandy Mining Ltd and controversy over QNI Ltd's merger plans with Gencor Ltd's Billiton Nickel.
"It throws up Australia as a very poorly managed corporate entity, especially on the resources side," he said, adding that BHP's share price could fall further on Monday.
"The market is resoundingly saying 'get me out'."
O'Connor's departure follows the resignation of the head of the group's minerals division, Dick Carter, on Wednesday and the head of its iron ore unit, Geoff Wedlock, on Thursday.
BHP closed down 45 cents at A$16.99 on heavy volume of more than nine million.
BHP chairman Jerry Ellis and chief executive John Prescott are due to hold a news conference at 5.15 p.m. (0715 GMT).
